Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research
ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how
generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. We introduce theCre-
ative AI Researcher (CAR), an agentic framework combining literature ground-
ing, iterative development and explicit conceptual operators. CAR constructs a
semantic knowledge graph from retrieved literature and equips an ideation agent
with graph-retrieval tools and four operators: bisociation, analogy, exploration and
elaboration. Each operator call is checked against structural acceptance conditions
and recorded, producing a trace of intermediate transformations and declared lit-
erature sources. We evaluate CAR with two language-model backbones across
40 LiveIdeaBench research topics and two execution benchmarks. CAR achieves
significantly higher

methodological novelty (MN) than single-shot prompting and
The AI Scientist. Its methodological novelty does not differ significantly from
the Research Ideation Agent, while its feasibility scores are higher on both back-
bones. With a shared experiment executor, CAR achieves the highest pairwise
win rate among the evaluated AI methods on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena.
In a ten-condition ablation study, MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step
proposal on both backbones, but no MN contrast survives correction for multi-
ple comparisons. The results do not establish a consistent quality benefit from

ations and declared literature sources inspectable, separating judged idea quality
from procedural traceability.

benefit from explicit operators beyond
free-form iteration. The operators provide a recorded sequence of graph edits and declared literature
sources.
Our contributions are:
• A decomposition of AI research ideation into literature grounding, iterative development and ex-
plicit creative operators. A ten-condition study on two backbones examines iteration and the op-
erator layer within this grounded setting, distinguishing their effects on judged idea quality from
the procedural trace they provide.
• CAR, which makes the decomposition testable: four creativity processes implemented as vali-
dated, recorded operators over a literature-derived knowledge graph, so that every proposal carries
a trace from prior work to the final idea.
• An evaluation of CAR on originality and effectiveness, the two criteria of the standard definition
of creativity, on three benchmarks, with judge agreement

LiveIdeaBench(Ruan et al., 2026) contains 1,180 scientific keywords from 22 domains and uses
LLM judges to assess the ideas generated for a keyword along dimensions inspired by Guilford's
account of divergent thinking (Guilford, 1967):originality,feasibility,clarity(how understandable
and complete an idea is) andfluency(how distinct a method's ideas for one keyword are from one
another). We select 40 keywords, ten each from the computational, physical, life and social sciences.
We report its fifth dimension, flexibility, in Appendix E.2. Our modifications to the protocol are
listed in Appendix C.1.
FML-bench(Zou et al., 2026) comprises 18 machine learning research tasks in 10 domains, each
with a baseline repository, a set of editable files and a held-out test metric, and scores an agent
on how far it improves the baseline. All agents edit code and run experiments through the

benchmark-provided tools, so differences between agents reflect their research strategy rather than
their tooling. We use theLitesplit of eight tasks.
BioXArena(Li et al., 2026a) is a benchmark of 76 end-to-end biomedical machine learning tasks
spanning nine areas, most combining several input modalities. Unlike FML-bench, a task supplies
data and a metric but no baseline repository, so an agent must design the pipeline and the method.
We use the ten tasks of the benchmark's human-comparison pilot, which supplies a human reference.
One task, cell-type-from-expression, has a label leak that makes it trivially solvable (five of seven
entries, including CAR and the human reference, score1.000). We show it but exclude it from
means and win rates.

evidence.excerpt:
LiveIdeaBench.We follow the benchmark's LLM-as-a-judge protocol, with its prompts, scales and
fluency score map. A panel of three critics from vendors other than the generators' scores each idea
1–10for originality (O), feasibility (F) and clarity (C), and judges fluency (Flu.) on every pair of a
method's five ideas for each keyword.
Because a critic judges originality from memory, we add amethodological novelty(MN) judge that
grounds the judgment in retrieved prior work. Each idea is converted to an approximately250-
word abstract. Related papers are retrieved from Semantic Scholar with the iterative query loop
of Si et al. (2025) under a publication-date cut-off, ranked by its LLM relevance score with ties
broken by SPECTER2 similarity (Singh et al., 2023), and the top10are kept. The same three judges
then apply the Stratified Novelty Judge of Shen et al. (2026), adapted from

evidence.excerpt:
CAR combines literature grounding, iterative development and explicit creative operators for re-
search ideation. It exceeds single-shot prompting and The AI Scientist in methodological novelty
and achieves the highest win rate among the evaluated AI methods on both execution benchmarks.
MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step proposal on both backbones, although no MN abla-
tion contrast survives correction for multiple comparisons. The operators make idea development
inspectable, but their quality benefit beyond free-form iteration is not established.
Limitations.Traces establish procedural provenance, not causal necessity. Judge agreement is
assessed on proposals used in MN evaluator development, without human quality ratings of our
ideas. Retrieval, extraction errors and limited execution tasks constrain the findings (Appendix J).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Downstream execution on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena with a shared external executor provides an objective measurement that corroborates the headline effectiveness claim.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: LLM judge panels for originality, feasibility, and methodological novelty, plus external benchmark execution metrics.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Structural acceptance conditions and validation rules applied to knowledge graph edits during iterative proposal generation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: While claims of improved auditability and competitive benchmark scores are documented, the headline premise that explicit structured operators improve ideation quality beyond iterative prompting is directly qualified by insignificant ablation contrasts.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation covers LLM-judged originality, feasibility, and methodological novelty across 40 LiveIdeaBench topics alongside empirical execution on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena. However, the critical ablation study shows that no methodological novelty gain over free-form iteration or unvalidated operations survives multiple testing corrections, leaving the specific benefit of the formal operators unverified.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Downstream empirical code execution results on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena tasks using a shared external executor.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Independent LLM-as-a-judge panels (Claude Sonnet, Gemini Pro, DeepSeek Pro) evaluating originality, feasibility, and methodological novelty, along with downstream code execution metrics on external benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Precondition checks and acceptance rules enforced on knowledge graph edits during iterative proposal generation.

primary.limitations: The manuscript candidly acknowledges that traces demonstrate procedural history rather than causal mechanisms, that human validation of idea quality was not conducted on newly generated ideas, and that operator ablations showed no statistically significant quality advantage after correction.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology constructs a literature knowledge graph per topic and enforces graph editing via four conceptual operators whose preconditions are structurally checked. The system design is documented in detail, though the authors note that accepted operations provide structural provenance rather than causal necessity for final idea generation.
primary.quality_rationale: While thoroughly executed and transparently reported, the core methodological innovation—validated explicit creative operators—fails to establish a statistically significant performance benefit over simple free-form iteration in the ten-condition ablation study.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents CAR (Creative AI Researcher), a framework combining literature-based knowledge graph extraction with four structural creative operators (bisociation, analogy, exploration, elaboration) to generate auditable research proposals.

scholarly_quality.rationale: While thoroughly executed and transparently reported, the core methodological innovation—validated explicit creative operators—fails to establish a statistically significant performance benefit over simple free-form iteration in the ten-condition ablation study.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript candidly acknowledges that traces demonstrate procedural history rather than causal mechanisms, that human validation of idea quality was not conducted on newly generated ideas, and that operator ablations showed no statistically significant quality advantage after correction.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
